steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The portfolio is worth as much as the performance — it must be detailed, reflective and analytical.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Document EVERY stage: stimulus response, research, exploration, rehearsal, refinement, performance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Reflection: not just what you did, but WHY you did it and what you would change — show critical thinking.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Practitioner influence: explicitly show how Stanislavski, Brecht, Frantic Assembly etc. shaped your work.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What should you include in a devising portfolio to achieve a high mark? | Explain the difference between describing what you did and evaluating why you did it. Why is evaluation more important? | How would you document the influence of a practitioner on your devised piece?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Stimulus analysis, research evidence, exploration techniques used, rehearsal process, key decisions and their justification, practitioner influence with examples, reflection on strengths and weaknesse | Description: 'We used a freeze-frame.' Evaluation: 'We used a freeze-frame to mark the moment when the truth was revealed, creating a pause that allowed the audience to absorb the significance — this  | Name the practitioner; explain the specific technique or idea used; describe how you applied it in rehearsal; evaluate its effect on the final piece; analyse how it shaped the audience's experience.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: The portfolio is NOT a diary — it's an analytical document Always justify: WHAT you did + WHY you did it + WHAT EFFECT it had Use practitioner terminology throughout — 'alienation effect', 'given circumstances' Include evidence: photos, diagrams, annotated scripts
